checks.method: Run the complete fixed CC-013 test before creating the authorized feature input tree.
checks.observed: The run produced exactly 6 failures. The inventory was empty and every other failure was FileNotFoundError for an authorized absent input; there was no semantic mismatch or unrelated failure.

checks.method: Enumerate the fixed source-owner inventory and inspect every member without following links.
checks.observed: Exactly 11 sorted cases own 18 unique regular, non-symlink JSON-shaped source members below the authorized feature_cases/inputs prefix. No separate input-manifest grammar was added.

checks.method: Compare all retained CC-X01 source members with the immutable research cases by raw bytes, byte length, and SHA-256.
checks.observed: All 9 retained source texts are copied exactly. Their evidence classifications and observations remain in CC-X01; CC-013 adds no replacement measurement or result label.

checks.method: Map each fixed case in the source-owner test to existing requirement IDs and resolve them against the CC-018 registry.
checks.observed: All 11 cases map only to the four existing linkml-support-profile requirement IDs: metamorphic, parity, positive, and refusal. No requirement, scenario, corpus row, output, or oracle is created by the mapping.

checks.method: Inspect the two neutral two-module duplicate-declaration bundles without executing a compiler or assigning an outcome.
checks.observed: One bundle contains equal source structure after removing only descriptions and literal annotations.adopts true; the other contains an unmarked structurally different range. Both use the neutral shared_value symbol and contain no expected decision, diagnostic, fact, or artifact.

checks.method: Parse the paired source members strictly and compare only their named source dimensions.
checks.observed: The input tree isolates equivalent numeric lexemes, defaulted versus explicit range, presentation-only changes, authored false, and mixin-order reversal. It records stimuli only, never expected semantic values.

checks.method: Run tests/contract_compiler/test_feature_isolation_inputs.py and scoped Ruff against the final fixed bytes.
checks.observed: All 7 fixed tests passed and scoped Ruff passed.

checks.method: Run the CC-013, CC-018, CC-010, retained CC-X01, and retained CC-X02 tests together.
Run the local CI test profile after all three independent input-owner trees are frozen.
checks.observed: Ruff passed; the configured suite passed 1,823 tests with 2 skips; all 66 contract-compiler tests passed; the 197-entry overseer ledger, 66-workstream integration state with 27 cards and 4 selections, and all 40 GraphRecipe tests passed. An earlier run with identical test results was deliberately refused by repository-purity detection because peer input bytes changed during execution.

checks.method: Review the exact CC-013 scope against package, runtime, compiler, corpus-publication, and release boundaries.
checks.observed: PACKAGE NOT_APPLICABLE. CC-013 adds repository-local input stimuli, one fixed test, and this report; it changes no distribution, installed data, public API, compiler, runtime, artifact, corpus membership, checksum, Docker image, or release claim.

limitations: CC-013 owns input stimuli only. Names and requirement references describe the feature under test; they are not compiler outcomes, oracle values, diagnostic identifiers, expected facts, or production-policy claims.

The 9 CC-X01 sources preserve immutable research bytes, but CC-X01 remains the authority for its measurements and classifications. The two CC-X02-derived bundles are unexecuted source stimuli, not new evidence about current ontologies.

Direct-fact conformance input remains with CC-017. Closed-composition wire values, operation traces, compiler and runtime behavior, public APIs, packages, Docker, releases, and every CC-R stage remain outside CC-013.
The input members remain absent from corpus.json and checksums.json. A later integration owner must review independent CC-014 oracles before publishing feature-case membership.
